## Overview

Add a regression test for a request arriving through EngineCore's input queue after an empty poll, while an uncapped lone-prefill batch is pending. This follow-up was discussed [with the author of #60485](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60485#issuecomment-6074742668).

Depends on #60485. The stack now includes its latest `5724f13` revision, merged with `main` at `08a65e287e` in `ccfaaacdf2`, followed by the replayed test commit `c015cba466`. The comparison against `main` includes the prerequisite changes; this follow-up's own test commit changes only `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py`. This PR stays in Draft until #60485 merges, then the test commit will be moved onto the updated `main` and revalidated.

## Claims

- Cover both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling through the production input-queue dispatch, scheduler, and GPU model execution.
- Verify that no extra batch is scheduled before the pending uncapped prefill is drained, and that the next poll admits the newcomer before scheduling again.
- Verify that the long request is capped again: with a token budget of 10 and a threshold of 5, the next batch contains 5 tokens for the long request and 1 for the newcomer.

## Validation

Current synchronization checks (2026-10-17): `c015cba466`, based on #60485 at `5724f13` and `main` at `08a65e287e`.

- Complete file-scoped pre-commit passed for all six files in the stacked diff, including Ruff, typos, mypy, test tethering, and repository checks. `git diff --check` and Python syntax compilation also passed.
- The replay conflict was limited to imports. AST comparison confirms the new regression test function, including its parametrization, is unchanged from `d5914f2`.
- The integration preserves `main`'s deprecated `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks` compatibility field alongside `has_uncapped_lone_prefill`.
- Targeted pytest could not collect because the local macOS environment lacks `tblib`. This checkout also has no compiled `vllm._C` extension and CUDA is unavailable. No tests or GPU validation were completed for this new revision; the GPU results below apply only to the earlier commit.

```bash
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/Users/admin/.cache/pre-commit \
  /Users/admin/PyCharm/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run \
  --files tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  vllm/config/scheduler.py vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py vllm/v1/engine/core.py --show-diff-on-failure
```

The targeted pytest invocation used the same paths and `-k` selection shown below, with the local `.venv/bin/python`; it exited during conftest import with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tblib'`.

Prior GPU validation (2026-10-13): `d5914f209689a2cc4def8f56b518cfda2304f5da`, the unchanged test patch rebased onto #60485 at `2c829e1d722129c2523d35af66c3db7fbc495239`. These results have not been rerun on `c015cba466`.

Environment: RTX 3080 Ti (12 GB), Ubuntu 22.04.5, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and Transformers 5.19.0. Model: `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`, snapshot `9408c553e5c189a7dcdc5a5dbd2feb476b061759`. The source checkout was installed in editable mode with the CUDA extension loaded successfully.

| Run | Result | Deselected | Skipped | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before the negative control | 8 passed | 226 | 0 | 142.34 s |
| Guard disabled temporarily | 2 expected assertion failures | 23 | 0 | 31.57 s |
| Guard restored | 8 passed | 226 | 0 | 94.05 s |

The eight cases comprise four scheduler tests, two existing EngineCore tests, and the new input-queue test with `async_scheduling=False` and `True`. No phase had collection/runtime errors or skipped tests.

Command for the restored run (the first run used `positive-before.xml`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  -k 'long_prefill_threshold or input_queue_arrival_during_uncapped_prefill or engine_core_no_schedule_ahead_of_uncapped_lone_prefill or engine_core_concurrent_batches' \
  -vv -ra --durations=8 --timeout=180 \
  --junitxml=/root/autodl-tmp/pr60796-validation/results/positive-after.xml
```

For the negative control, temporarily setting only `can_schedule_ahead = True` in EngineCore made both new cases fail at `Scheduled ahead of the uncapped prefill`: `schedule()` was called twice instead of once. The guard was restored byte-for-byte before rerunning all eight cases. This was a targeted guard mutation.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  -k input_queue_arrival_during_uncapped_prefill \
  -vv -ra --durations=8 --timeout=180 \
  --junitxml=/root/autodl-tmp/pr60796-validation/results/negative-control.xml
```

Environment exception: `arctic-inference==0.1.1` was excluded from a derived copy of the test requirements because its isolated build pins `torch==2.7.0`, unavailable in the cu130 index. The selected suite does not enable suffix decoding, all eight cases ran, and repository requirements were unchanged.

The complete file-scoped pre-commit run passed on the rebased test file, including Ruff, typos, mypy, and repository checks. The current baseline's mypy hook targets Python 3.11. `git diff --check` also passed. The pre-commit command used a separate local lint environment:

```bash
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/private/tmp/pr60485-pre-commit \
  /private/tmp/pr60485-checks/.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run \
  --files tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py --show-diff-on-failure
```

The existing Buildkite `engine-1-gpu` job selects `tests/v1/engine/`. These results are local validation; upstream GPU CI is still pending.

## Details

The test reuses `DummyExecutor` and the existing request helper. It initializes an `EngineCoreProc` with in-process queues and manually drives the production poll/step methods without starting ZMQ threads. Events hold the executor's single worker until a receiver thread has enqueued the newcomer at the first batch's result-wait boundary. This fixes the ordering without sleep-based timing; arrival is controlled while the batch result is pending.

The long prompt has 24 tokens, leaving 14 after its first 10-token chunk. The later 5-token allocation therefore demonstrates that the threshold is reapplied to the original request. Requests are drained to completion, and cleanup releases the executor and shuts it down in `finally`.

#60485's existing EngineCore test adds the second request directly to the scheduler after draining the first batch. This follow-up covers arrival through the input queue between polling and draining. Searches for `60476 in:body` and `input_queue prefill`, rechecked on 2026-10-17 alongside the issue discussion, found only #60485 and this PR among open PRs.

The follow-up changes only test code. HTTP/ZMQ transport, suffix decoding, model-quality evaluation, and latency/throughput measurements are outside this validation's scope; no performance claim is made.

AI assistance: The original test and the 2026-10-17 synchronization were prepared with assistance from OpenAI Codex. The original submission records human review and the CUDA EngineCore runs on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti. Current synchronization checks and their limitations are listed separately above; no new GPU result is claimed.

Read through ac38173. The semantics line up with what #60485 guarantees: the arrival that lands while the uncapped batch is in flight misses this poll, `schedule` is not called again until the pending batch drains, and on the next step the long request is capped back to the threshold while the newcomer gets its first chunk. The two-variant parametrization over async_scheduling is the right matrix since the batch-queue path differs there.

One small thing I checked while reading: if `waiting_for_output.wait(30)` ever timed out, the assertion fails inside the receiver thread but `release_execution.set()` still runs in the finally, so the engine step cannot deadlock on a hung test. Nice failure mode.

Thanks for taking a close look, especially at the timeout cleanup! Glad the test lines up with the behavior you intended. I’ll keep this in draft for now, then rebase and rerun the tests once #60485 lands.

Thanks for the detailed walkthrough! I’ll leave those bounds as they are for now. Once #60485 lands, I’ll rebase, rerun the GPU validation, and post the updated commit and results here. Appreciate you offering to take another look!

@Ondre119 Thanks for driving this through. I walked the test against the actual `step_with_batch_queue` flow and it pins exactly the contract from #60485:

Step 1 leaves the queue empty and returns early (spy=1), because `can_schedule_ahead` sees `batch_queue[0].has_uncapped_lone_prefill` after the uncapped chunk lands. Step 2 is where the regression would show: with the old `if self.scheduler.has_requests()` check, the mid-step arrival would trigger a second `schedule()` while batch 1 sits in the queue, and `spy.call_count == 1` fails. So the assertion set (call counts, `batch_queue` drain, `"short" not in requests`, `num_computed_tokens == 10`) would all break without the fix, and the re-cap `{"long": 5, "short": 1}` on the next poll confirms the threshold re-engages once the arrival is visible.

The timing control is clean: patching `first_future.result` to gate on the receiver thread makes the mid-step arrival deterministic, and the `finally` blocks plus the 30s timeouts keep a broken run from hanging. The `EngineCoreProc.__new__` + manual attribute injection matches the harness style already used in this file for avoiding ZMQ I/O threads.

Two small nits, neither blocking:

1. `blocker = core.model_executor.thread_pool.submit(release_execution.wait, 30)` — the 30s here is the Event-wait timeout that becomes the blocking delay if `receive_newcomer` fails its assert, which is fine, but if the DummyExecutor finishes faster than the event you get a spurious pass path only on timeouts. Not a real concern given the `assert blocker.result(timeout=30)` afterwards.
2. After the final `core._process_engine_step()`, the drain loop runs up to 20 iterations but the engine actually needs only a handful (long has 24-15=9 tokens left, then decode for both). If the loop were ever to time out on `has_work()`, a failing assertion would point at a scheduler stall rather than this PR's surface. Fine as written.

One process note for when #60485 lands: please do rebase the test commit onto the updated main and rerun the GPU validation you reported, exactly as your body says. I will re-check the assertions once more against the rebased commit.

LGTM as the regression test for the input-queue path.

This fills the level the scheduler unit tests in #60485 cannot reach: a real input-queue arrival landing while the lone prefill is mid-chunk, asserting the newcomer is not scheduled ahead of it.

Read through the whole diff. Determinism is handled the right way with Events instead of sleeps, the waits are bounded so a regression hangs fail loudly instead of wedging CI, and parametrizing over async_scheduling covers both step paths. The assertions match the invariant exactly: {"long": 10} immediately after the uncapped chunk, {"long": 5, "short": 1} after drain.

I cannot execute this locally (macOS CPU source checkout, no compiled _C extension, module CUDA-gated), so leaving this as a comment rather than an approval. From reading, this looks good to me.

@@ -1195,6 +1195,23 @@ def test_long_prefill_threshold_ignored_when_alone():
 
     output = scheduler.schedule()
     assert output.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] == 1024
+    # The engine must not schedule ahead of this uncapped chunk.
+    assert output.has_uncapped_lone_prefill
+
+
+def test_long_prefill_threshold_short_step_keeps_schedule_ahead():
+    """A lone request whose chunk stays within the threshold does not block
+    scheduling the next batch behind it."""
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        max_num_batched_tokens=1024,
+        long_prefill_token_threshold=400,
+    )
+    request = create_requests(num_requests=1, num_tokens=300)[0]
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] == 300
+    assert not output.has_uncapped_lone_prefill
 
 
 def test_long_prefill_threshold_applies_with_other_requests():

     output = scheduler.schedule()

     )
 
 
+def make_request_with_max_tokens(req_id: str, max_tokens: int) -> EngineCoreRequest:
+    request = make_request()
+    request.request_id = req_id
+    request.sampling_params.max_tokens = max_tokens
+    return request
+
+
+class DummyExecutor(UniProcExecutor):
+    """Executor whose execute_model/sample_tokens run on a thread pool, so
+    tests can drive the concurrent-batch queue without blocking."""
+
+    def initialize_from_config(self, kv_cache_configs: list[KVCacheConfig]) -> None:
+        super().initialize_from_config(kv_cache_configs)
+
+        # Create a thread pool with a single worker
+        self.thread_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
+
+    def execute_model(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output,
+        non_block=False,
+    ) -> Future[ModelRunnerOutput | None]:
+        """Make execute_model non-blocking."""
+        # DummyExecutor used only for testing async case.
+        assert non_block
+
+        def _execute():
+            output = self.collective_rpc("execute_model", args=(scheduler_output,))
+            # Make a copy because output[0] may be reused
+            # by the next batch.
+            return copy.deepcopy(output[0])
+
+        # Use the thread pool instead of creating a new thread
+        return self.thread_pool.submit(_execute)
+
+    def sample_tokens(
+        self, grammar_output, non_block=False
+    ) -> Future[ModelRunnerOutput]:

+    core.engines_running = False

+        set_default_torch_num_threads(1),

+            core,
+            vllm_config=engine_args.create_engine_config(),
+            log_stats=False,
+            executor_class=DummyExecutor,
+        )
+
+    release_execution = Event()
+    waiting_for_output = Event()
+    try:
+        long_req = make_request_with_max_tokens("long", 2)
+        long_req.prompt_token_ids = PROMPT_TOKENS * 2
+        assert len(long_req.prompt_token_ids) == 24
+        short_req = make_request_with_max_tokens("short", 2)
+        short_req.prompt_token_ids = PROMPT_TOKENS[:1]
+        newcomer = core.preprocess_add_request(short_req)
+        core.input_queue.put_nowait(
+            (EngineCoreRequestType.ADD, core.preprocess_add_request(long_req))
+        )
+        core._process_input_queue()
+        blocker = core.model_executor.thread_pool.submit(release_execution.wait, 30)
+
+        with patch.object(
+            core.scheduler, "schedule", wraps=core.scheduler.schedule
+        ) as spy:
+            core._process_engine_step()
+            assert core.batch_queue is not None

+            assert first_batch.num_scheduled_tokens == {"long": 10}
+            assert not first_future.done()

+                ):

+                arrival.result(timeout=30)

+            assert blocker.result(timeout=30)
+            assert spy.call_count == 1, "Scheduled ahead of the uncapped prefill"
+            assert not core.batch_queue

+            assert "short" not in core.scheduler.requests
+            assert core.scheduler.requests["long"].num_computed_tokens == 10
+            assert core.scheduler.requests["long"].num_tokens == 24
+
+            core._process_input_queue()
+            assert core.input_queue.empty()
+            core._process_engine_step()
+            assert spy.call_count == 2
+            assert core.batch_queue[0][1].num_scheduled_tokens == {
+                "long": 5,
+                "short": 1,
+            }
+
+        for _ in range(20):
+            if not core.has_work():
+                break
+            core._process_input_queue()
+            core._process_engine_step()
+        assert not core.has_work()
+    finally:
+        release_execution.set()
+        core.model_executor.thread_pool.shutdown(wait=True)
+        core.shutdown()

@Ondre119 Thanks for driving this through. I walked the test against the actual `step_with_batch_queue` flow and it pins exactly the contract from #60485:

Step 1 leaves the queue empty and returns early (spy=1), because `can_schedule_ahead` sees `batch_queue[0].has_uncapped_lone_prefill` after the uncapped chunk lands. Step 2 is where the regression would show: with the old `if self.scheduler.has_requests()` check, the mid-step arrival would trigger a second `schedule()` while batch 1 sits in the queue, and `spy.call_count == 1` fails. So the assertion set (call counts, `batch_queue` drain, `"short" not in requests`, `num_computed_tokens == 10`) would all break without the fix, and the re-cap `{"long": 5, "short": 1}` on the next poll confirms the threshold re-engages once the arrival is visible.

The timing control is clean: patching `first_future.result` to gate on the receiver thread makes the mid-step arrival deterministic, and the `finally` blocks plus the 30s timeouts keep a broken run from hanging. The `EngineCoreProc.__new__` + manual attribute injection matches the harness style already used in this file for avoiding ZMQ I/O threads.

Two small nits, neither blocking:

1. `blocker = core.model_executor.thread_pool.submit(release_execution.wait, 30)` — the 30s here is the Event-wait timeout that becomes the blocking delay if `receive_newcomer` fails its assert, which is fine, but if the DummyExecutor finishes faster than the event you get a spurious pass path only on timeouts. Not a real concern given the `assert blocker.result(timeout=30)` afterwards.
2. After the final `core._process_engine_step()`, the drain loop runs up to 20 iterations but the engine actually needs only a handful (long has 24-15=9 tokens left, then decode for both). If the loop were ever to time out on `has_work()`, a failing assertion would point at a scheduler stall rather than this PR's surface. Fine as written.

One process note for when #60485 lands: please do rebase the test commit onto the updated main and rerun the GPU validation you reported, exactly as your body says. I will re-check the assertions once more against the rebased commit.
